Less than a year after using her considerable psychic abilities to wrench herself backwards through time, Vanessa Long could feel the impact of her actions. She constantly ached, fought against daily migraines, and her mind was scattered - focusing on this time and reality grew more difficult with each passing day. Worst of all, the dark version of herself which had "hitched a ride" on her jaunt through time fed off her pain. 

All it took was the right amount of stress. In battle against the dreaded GloomWeaver, The Visionary wrapped herself in a telekinetic cocoon in order to avoid a swarm of arcane cultists, but when she did so, her fellow heroes heard a muffled scream from within the glowing purple energy barrier. It shattered with a burst of green energy, throwing cultists about like rag dolls. A pale, maniacally grinning Vanessa Long strode forth, waving a dismissive gesture at GloomWeaver, which banished him from this realm entirely.

"Hello, dearies," Visionary cooed. "Let's go save the Multiverse . . . "

That's the entire premise of the Thorathian rebelion we see in the WotC environment deck. Voss having a promo now just wouldn't make much sense story wise. Voss will be back, Christopher said as much, but it won't be until later in the Tactics storyline.

phantaskippy:

Doesn't mean someone else can't take over, maybe he has a child?

There are several things that we know about Grand Warlord Voss.

  1. He was the second son of the Thorathian ruling family.  Presumably, this means that there was a first son somewhere.

  2. He returns to Dok'Thorath at the head of an army, and while he declares himself the new ruler after a coup, there is no (explicit) mention of the fate of his older brother (presumably the heir to the throne), the former Sovereign, or the rest of the ruling family.

  3. At the time the Prime Wardens Visit, Dok'Thorath is in a state of open rebellion, with street fighting and numerous factions vying for power.  There is still no mention of a new Sovereign.

Put it all together, and it seems like it would be entirely possible that we could get a promo, not of Voss, but of someone else in the ruling family-in-exile.  Or we coudl see one of Voss's Lieutenants take power, or one of the admirals of the remnant fleet. It could be minion against minion, ship against ship, with Earth caught in the middle of a civil war.  After all, there are no cards in Voss's deck that actually mention his name, so theres no need to keep him around.  Or it coudl be that Voss has a son of his own that is coming to collect the tattered remains of the Thorathian Conquest Fleet.   

Basically, I think your idea is totally awesome.

posts.cooked:
If we assume story reasons for promos and no doubling on promos we can make a list of likely canidates.

 

Vilains who already have promos

Blade

Omnitron

Gloom weaver

Spite

 

Villains whose story is already being advanced by Villains

Miss Information

Plague Rat

Ambuscade

La Capitan

 

Villains who are new enough a promo already seems unliley

Kaagra

Infinitor

Wager Master

Progeny

Deadline

 

This leaves us with

Akash'Bhuta

Kismet

Apostate

Voss

Dreamer

Dawn

Ennead

Chairman

Matriarch

Iron Legacy

Vengeful Five

 

Vengeful Five is highly unlikely, their place in the story is established and unlikely to evolve (after all they were briught together by Blade who is out of commision until Tactics due to the side effects of his boosting serum). Chairman is unlikely, the organization is crushed and he disappears until Tactics. Dreamer is unlikely, mostly because poor vanessa long is already suffered a lot and her place in the story would likely be a one off deal. Same with Iron Legacy, The Ennead and Matriarch. Iron Legacy was dealt with and should not return, The Ennead cause Horus Ra who then came back and beat them, seems little ground for a resurgence that would alter how they play and Matriarch probably won't get a promo because her change is to become a hero in Tactics.

 

This brings us to Akash'Bhuta, Kismet, Apostate, Voss, and  Dawn.

 

Voss would be awesome, coming back from the Realm of Discord to take Vengeance on Earth, but I feel that's going to be in Tactics because we've been told we won't recognize him and a promo doesn't change how a deck plays to that extreme, especially one as tight as Voss. (Tangent: Could Voss be the Mist taking people in Tactics, using them to build a new army before marching forth?)

Dawn would be good, but Hammer and Anvil appear in Villians so it's at best 50/50 in my mind.

Kismet could be, but I doubt it. She's a pain and a trickster, kind of like Joker. She keeps coming back but she doesn't change much overall.

 

So my money would go on Akash'Bhuta and Apostate. Akash we know changes by Tactics, those purple crystals everywhere and it's likely that started before Tactics. Also Akash'Bhuta can be a fun fight but I've never felt her flipping really meant anything and she is too easy in environments with little or no targets (fighting her in the Freedom Tower is almost boring). I think a promo to make her more active and a more devastating threat would be good. Apostate is almost the obvious one, we know there is a lot about his story that is unclear and needs to be revealed. A promo for him is almost a must to clear up what his deal actually is.

posts.name: phantaskippy
posts.cooked:
So likelihood of a new promo:  Phantaskippy's top 5.

1.  Apostate:  His deck works so well and his Character card is so easy to change up, and his storyline has to be a thing that continues.

2.  Voss:  I just can't imagine Wrath having two Thorathian decks not somehow leading to a revival of the army, plus with that engine the character card could go anywhere.

3.  Dreamer:  Would really work well.  We know she's still around, and the possibility that Visionary alters her own timeline substantially after the "Fixed Point" could lead to all kinds of fun.  As a minion heavy deck there could be all kinds of difference.

4.  Kismet:  Less for storyline and later importance, more off deck mechanics, her deck could be very different with a promo.

5.  Wager Master:  I thought it in playtesting and still do, this deck seems set up for a promo.  Or maybe I'm crazy.  I also don't see one coming with the last expansion.  I could see him ending up a servant of the big bad after finally being defeated.  It could be wierd.

 

I don't see Akash or Matriarch Happening, largely because their character cards are so heavily invested in the engine that makes them run.  There isn't a lot of room to redirect that engine to another purpose.
